claims.feature: other: digressive potted histories of minor figures
claims.claim: Auden says Kay spins off additional stories at tangents to show that side characters' stories are equally valid.
claims.source: Sandy Auden, review of The Last Light of the Sun, infinity plus
claims.quote: the stories of side characters are equally valid

claims.feature: other: history as material rather than subject
claims.claim: Kirkus says Kay is less interested in re-creating history than in playing the changes on the epic themes of love, war and destiny.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews, unsigned review of A Song for Arbonne
claims.quote: Kay is less interested in re-creating history than in playing

claims.claim: Kirkus says Kay's usual elements include prose that sometimes gets carried away with itself.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews, unsigned review of A Brightness Long Ago, issue of 15 March 2019
claims.quote: prose that sometimes gets carried away with itself

claims.feature: other: a world a quarter-turn from ours
claims.claim: Publishers Weekly says Kay creates a realm that resembles ours but is just different enough to enrich the fantasy genre.
claims.source: Publishers Weekly, unsigned review of A Song for Arbonne
claims.quote: a realm that resembles ours but is just different enough

claims.feature: other: fidelity to sources with deliberate changes
claims.claim: The Strange Horizons companion says Kay works closely with his historical sources but sometimes makes crucial changes in the course of events.

claims.quote: he sometimes makes crucial changes in the course of events

claims.claim: Attebery's Strategies of Fantasy contains no occurrence of the string Gavriel, and none of Tigana, Fionavar, Arbonne or Al-Rassan, so the book does not discuss Guy Gavriel Kay.
claims.source: Brian Attebery, Strategies of Fantasy (Indiana University Press, 1992), full OCR text counted by the finder

claims.claim: The only occurrence of the surname Kay in Attebery's Strategies of Fantasy is an index entry for the folklorist Kay Stone at page ninety-three.
claims.source: Brian Attebery, Strategies of Fantasy (Indiana University Press, 1992), index

claims.feature: other: personalised history instead of names and dates
claims.claim: Dominic Cilli says Under Heaven gives a history lesson where the names and dates are not tucked neatly in a row but a more personalized history.
claims.source: Dominic Cilli, review of Under Heaven, SF Site, 2010
claims.quote: names and dates are tucked neatly in a row

claims.feature: other: the north as a plainer register than the courts
claims.claim: Hromic says Kay's northern novel visits a corner of his milieu far more raw and earthy than the rarefied decadence of Sarantium.
claims.source: Alma A. Hromic, review of The Last Light of the Sun, SF Site, 2004
claims.quote: far more raw and earthy than the rarefied decadence

claims.feature: other: architecture of the whole narrative
claims.claim: Barbour says the overarching plan of the narrative is grand but not grandiose, complex but not needlessly complicated.
claims.source: Doug Barbour, review of The Lions of Al-Rassan for The Edmonton Journal (reprinted BrightWeavings)
claims.quote: grand but not grandiose, complex but not needlessly complicated

claims.claim: Kilheffer names the sentence 'They had been dealt with' on the first page as a line with a distinctly contemporary feel.
claims.source: Rob Kilheffer, review of The Lions of Al-Rassan for Fantasy & Science Fiction (reprinted BrightWeavings)
claims.quote: a line with a distinctly contemporary feel

claims.claim: The Encyclopedia of Fantasy, as quoted on this page, says of Kay's work on The Silmarillion that he seems to have learned from the experience.
claims.source: BrightWeavings relaying The Encyclopedia of Fantasy (attributed on the page to Peter Kuzca)
claims.quote: seems to have learned from the experience

claims.claim: Jo Walton says the physical details of the Sarantine Mosaic are all real enough to bite.
claims.source: Jo Walton, reread of the Sarantine Mosaic (originally Tor.com, reprinted BrightWeavings)
claims.quote: The details are all real enough to bite

claims.claim: Walton says there is more use of the pluperfect tense in these two books than in anything else she can think of.
claims.source: Jo Walton, reread of the Sarantine Mosaic (originally Tor.com, reprinted BrightWeavings)
claims.quote: more use of the pluperfect tense in these than anything

claims.feature: other: naming that does not hide its original

claims.quote: Kay isn't trying to hide the fact that Sarantium is Byzantium

verdicts.trueWording: the stories of side characters are equally valid
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (infinityplus.co.uk, live, 200). Story-structure paragraph: Kay 'even manages to spin-off additional stories at tangents along the way' to show this. Signed Sandy Auden, 3 July 2005. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Kay is less interested in re-creating history than in playing
verdicts.note: Raw Kirkus page fetched live (200). Review body sentence continues '...the changes on the epic themes of love, war, and destiny.' Kirkus Reviews Issue Nov. 1, 1992. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: prose that sometimes gets carried away with itself
verdicts.note: Raw Kirkus page fetched live (200). Last sentence of the review body lists 'his usual elements in play' and ends with this phrase. Page states 'Kirkus Reviews Issue: March 15, 2019', matching the cited issue.

verdicts.trueWording: a realm that resembles ours but is just different enough
verdicts.note: Raw PW page fetched live (200), ISBN 978-0-517-59312-7, reviewed 11/30/1992. Closing sentence of the review body: Kay 'creates a vivid world...' in such a realm, '...to enrich the fantasy genre.' All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: he sometimes makes crucial changes in the course of events
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (20160319104019id_) fetched, 200. Sentence sits in the 'History Intro' section and opens by saying Kay works closely with his historical sources, but... Both limbs supported. The capture carries no byline, so the Cobb/Mohanraj attribution is not confirmed by the page itself.

verdicts.trueWording: Zero hits: Gavriel, Tigana, Fionavar, Arbonne, Al-Rassan; 'Guy' also absent
verdicts.note: Full OCR downloaded from archive.org (200, 458,049 bytes, matching the cited size) and counted with grep -oic: Gavriel 0, Tigana 0, Fionavar 0, Arbonne 0, Al-Rassan 0, Rassan 0, Sarantium 0; no word-boundary 'Guy'. Claim carries no quotation, so verbatim grading does not apply; the counting claim and its inference are confirmed by execution on the raw text.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'the only occurrence' - there are TWO occurrences of 'Kay' in the text, and 'Kay' is Kay Stone's forename, not a surname
verdicts.trueWording: Index: 'Stone, Kay, 93'; Works Cited also lists 'Stone, Kay.'
verdicts.note: Same raw OCR, grep -nE '\bKay\b' returns exactly two lines: 8507 in Works Cited (a Kay Stone entry on Walt Disney, in Women and Folklore) and 9168 in the Index ('Stone, Kay, 93'). So the page-93 index entry for the folklorist Kay Stone is real and is the only INDEX occurrence, but not the only occurrence in the book, and 'Kay' there is a given name, not a surname.

verdicts.trueWording: names and dates are tucked neatly in a row
verdicts.note: Live host sfsite.com is dead (NXDOMAIN on 8.8.8.8), so reached via Wayback raw capture 20250131133314id_ (200). Review body says it may not be a history lesson where the names and dates sit so, but a more personalized history of eighth-century China. Signed Dominic Cilli, 2010. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: far more raw and earthy than the rarefied decadence
verdicts.note: sfsite.com is NXDOMAIN; reached via Wayback raw capture 20251014060325id_ (200). Body calls it the book Kay has called his 'Northern novel', visiting a corner of that milieu that is this - and says 'of a Sarantine Empire', not 'Sarantium', a naming variation with the same referent. Signed Alma A. Hromic, 2004.

verdicts.trueWording: grand but not grandiose, complex but not needlessly complicated
verdicts.note: Raw brightweavings.com/revlions/ fetched live (200). Section headed 'Review by Doug Barbour, for The Edmonton Journal'; the sentence reads 'the overarching plan of the whole narrative is' this. Claim drops only the word 'whole'. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: a line with a distinctly contemporary feel
verdicts.note: Same raw page, section headed as a review by Rob Kilheffer for Fantasy & Science-Fiction Magazine: on the very first page, of some guards, 'They had been dealt with' - then the quoted phrase. Both the quoted sentence and the first-page limb are exact substrings of the page.

verdicts.trueWording: seems to have learned from the experience
verdicts.note: Raw brightweavings.com/leatherboundtiganaintro/ fetched live (200). Opening paragraph notes Kay helped Christopher Tolkien edit The Silmarillion in the 1970s, then attributes the quoted phrase to Peter Kuzca writing in The Encyclopedia of Fantasy - the page's own attribution, as the claim states.

verdicts.trueWording: The details are all real enough to bite
verdicts.note: Raw brightweavings.com/revsarantium/ fetched live (200). In the section 'Review by Jo Walton. This review originally appeared here at tor.com'; the sentence continues with the tesserae, mud and fish sauces, so 'physical details' is supported.

verdicts.trueWording: more use of the pluperfect tense in these than anything
verdicts.note: Same raw page, Walton section, paragraph on pacing (which it calls unusual, concentrating on single days with flashbacks). 'These' is the two-book Sarantine Mosaic under review, so the two-books limb holds; the sentence ends 'else I can think of.'

verdicts.trueWording: Kay isn't trying to hide the fact that Sarantium is Byzantium
verdicts.note: Same raw page, opening paragraph of the Walton review. The page continues with Varena/Ravenna, Valerius/Justinian, Pertennius/Procopius and also Gisel/Amalasuntha; all four pairs in the claim are supported. Only difference from the cited quote is the curly apostrophe.
